title: Throughput ecosystem lab runner and customer onboarding validation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a repeatable, tenant-aware lab runner and a concise customer onboarding validation runbook that demonstrates Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees, exercise autoscaler policies under realistic noise, and produces artifacts for customer acceptance. This ticket encapsulates harness orchestration, workload generation (token/sequence-aware), KV-cache warmup scenarios, autoscaler stress sweeps, and the acceptance checklist used in handoffs to Solutions/CSRs.
acceptance_criteria: Lab runner can replay 3 canonical customer workload profiles (burst-heavy chat, long-context batch generation, mixed embeddings+chat) with >95% scenario fidelity versus recorded traces
Autoscaler policy sweep produces a stability map (sustained throughput, 99th tail latency, cost per token) for each policy variant and stores results in the console metrics bucket
KV-cache warmup routines reproduce observed cold-start tails and demonstrate >30% tail-latency improvement after warmup for chat workloads

Customer acceptance runbook contains step-by-step validation, required dashboards, PR checklist, and a signoff template; on first use, at least one customer pilot completes full signoff without engineering-side follow-ups
Artifacts (metrics CSVs, profiler traces, orchestration logs) are auto-uploaded and linked in the ticket for every run
implementation_notes: Runner implemented as a k8s-native orchestrator that schedules isolated tenant namespaces to avoid cross-tenant resource interference
Use existing prober lib for generating token-rate distributions but extend to support sequence-length skew and multi-request correlation to simulate KV cache reuse
Add a noise-injection module to simulate co-located batch jobs and GC pauses; noise profiles are parameterized for 'light', 'medium', 'heavy'
Integrate with Console to push experiment metadata and a synthetic 'throughput signature' metric visible on target model route dashboards
Store raw results in s3://redwood-lab-runs/<run-id>/ with deterministic naming for replayability
test_plan: Smoke: run single-tenant burst profile for 15 minutes against a canary model variant; verify no pod OOMs and tail latency < configured SLO
Regression: replay recorded customer trace from ENG-42199 and compare percentiles (p50, p95, p99, p999) within tolerance thresholds
Autoscaler sweep: run scaling grid (min=1,max=32,scale-window=30s/60s/120s) and chart stability windows; annotate policy combinations that cause oscillation
Warmup experiments: compare cold-run vs. post-warmup runs on token cache hit ratio and end-to-end latency
Cost-profile: compute per-token cost for each policy and add to report (GPU-hours, infra egress, scheduling overhead)
Failcase: intentionally saturate KV cache and validate fallback policy triggers (model variant switch or degraded mode) and recording of the incident in run artifacts
runbook_steps: Pre-run: confirm model variant is pinned and snapshot created; upload customer trace if available
Start run: choose workload profile, noise level, and autoscaler policy; launch run via /lab-runner API
Observe: open the run dashboard link; monitor throughput, request latencies, KV hit ratio, and pod-level CPU/GPU utilization
Validate: run acceptance checklist comparing measured metrics to promised throughput and latency thresholds
Collect artifacts: wait for orchestrator to upload logs, csvs, and profiler dumps; attach artifacts link to customer ticket
Signoff: if all checks pass, fill signoff template and request Solutions to confirm with customer; otherwise, file follow-up ENG tickets with reproducible seed
metrics_definitions: throughput_rps: total completed requests per second across the tenant namespace
token_throughput: tokens/sec emitted (generation tasks) aggregated per second
tail_latency_ms: p99 and p999 end-to-end request latency measured at ingress
kv_cache_hit_ratio: fraction of KV requests served from warm cache vs. regenerated
cost_per_k_generated: normalized infra cost (USD) per thousand generated tokens for the run
policy_stability_score: heuristic combining oscillation count and sustained throughput variance
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Synthetic workloads fail to capture customer correlation patterns -> Mitigation: prioritize adding customer-provided traces and enable sequence-correlation replay mode
Risk: Autoscaler oscillation in edge configs causing excessive GPU churn -> Mitigation: add hysteresis and backoff parameters; create 'safe-default' policy for customer demos
Risk: Large artifact uploads impact cluster egress budgets -> Mitigation: compress traces and allow RU-based retention policies; optional offload to partner buckets
Risk: Run determinism across k8s clusters -> Mitigation: pin cluster node types for validation and include cluster spec in run metadata
